# Rear differential locker bypass and switch install

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Take existing wiring apart and connect a custom switch or OTRATTW module into the circuit using crimp splices. [t70]

[Partial] Locate the factory differential position switch plug and disconnect the existing wiring harness. [t117]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Take the existing wiring harness apart to prepare for reconfiguration.
2. [Partial] Connect a custom switch or OTRATTW module into the circuit using crimp splices, ensuring connections are secure.
3. [Partial] Plug the connector back in and drive the vehicle to verify operation before visiting an auto parts store.

_Procedure reported by [t70]._

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Disconnect the battery before working on electrical connections to prevent blowing fuses. [t70]
- [Partial] Cut wires at least an inch back from the connector instead of flush to allow room for error if a wrong wire is cut. [t70]

## Common mistakes

- Accidentally cutting pin 22 too close to the connector, leaving only one side connected. [t70]
- [Partial] Starting the car without plugging in the harness first, causing communication errors. [t70]
- [Partial] Forgetting to reset ECU codes after disconnecting the battery. [t70]
